chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:

I complained to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) of a stomach ache that I had found, so he said to me: 'What prevents you from drinking the milk of cows?' He said to me: 'Do you drink it at all?' So I said to him: 'Yes, repeatedly.' He said: 'How do you find it?' So I said: 'I find it tanning the stomach, covering the two kidneys with fat, and making the food desirable.' He said to me: 'If it were its days, I and you would have gone out to Yanbu' until we drank it.'

key_terms.تَكْسُو الْكُلْيَتَيْنِ الشَّحْمَ: Covering the two kidneys with fat
key_terms.يَنْبُعَ: Yanbu', a place known for its milk

ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of cow's milk according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes cow's milk as a therapeutic remedy for the narrator's stomach ailment, highlighting its specific benefits for digestion, kidney health, and appetite. The Imam’s enthusiastic response—expressing a desire to travel to Yanbu to drink it if it were in season—underscores the high medicinal status of cow's milk in Shia medical tradition, distinguishing it from other dairy sources. This narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the Prophetic and Imami emphasis on natural dietary remedies for physical well-being.
